questions.question: A model that performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data is exhibiting which problem?
options: Underfitting (high bias)
Overfitting (high variance)
Irreducible error
Data drift
questions.explanation: Overfitting means the model has memorized the training data, including its noise, and fails to generalize to new data. This is characterized by low training error but high validation/test error, and it corresponds to high variance.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of unsupervised learning?
options: Predicting house prices from square footage
Classifying emails as spam or not-spam
Grouping customers into segments based on purchasing behavior
Training a robot to navigate a maze using rewards
questions.explanation: Customer segmentation is unsupervised learning because there are no predefined labels — the algorithm discovers groups on its own. Predicting prices and classifying spam are supervised tasks, while maze navigation is reinforcement learning.

questions.question: In the bias-variance decomposition, what does the 'irreducible noise' term represent?
options: Error caused by using too few features
Error caused by a model that is too complex
Inherent randomness in the data that no model can eliminate
Error introduced by incorrect hyperparameter choices
questions.explanation: Irreducible noise (also called Bayes error) is the inherent randomness in the data-generating process. Even a perfect model cannot reduce this component of the error. It sets a lower bound on achievable prediction error.

questions.question: Why should the test set NOT be used during model selection or hyperparameter tuning?
options: The test set is typically too small to give reliable scores
Using it would cause the model to train more slowly
It would lead to an optimistically biased estimate of generalization performance
Scikit-learn does not allow access to the test set during training
questions.explanation: If you use the test set to make modeling decisions (choosing hyperparameters, selecting between models), you are implicitly fitting to the test set. The resulting performance estimate will be optimistically biased and will not reflect true generalization to completely unseen data.

questions.question: In 5-fold cross-validation, how many times is each data point used for validation?
options: Once
Twice
Five times
It depends on the random seed
questions.explanation: In K-fold cross-validation, the data is split into K folds. Each fold serves as the validation set exactly once, while the remaining K-1 folds are used for training. So each data point appears in the validation set exactly one time across all K iterations.

questions.question: Which scenario indicates that a model is underfitting?
options: Training error is low, validation error is high
Training error is high, validation error is high
Training error is low, validation error is low
Training error is high, validation error is low
questions.explanation: Underfitting (high bias) means the model is too simple to capture the underlying pattern. It performs poorly everywhere — both on data it has seen (training) and data it has not (validation). Both errors are high.

questions.question: A supervised learning task where the output is a continuous numeric value is called:
options: Classification
Clustering
Regression
Dimensionality reduction
questions.explanation: Regression is the supervised learning task of predicting continuous numeric outputs (e.g., price, temperature, score). Classification predicts discrete categories. Clustering and dimensionality reduction are unsupervised tasks.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST effective strategy to combat overfitting?
options: Remove regularization to let the model learn freely
Train for more epochs without any stopping criterion
Collect more training data
Increase the polynomial degree of the model
questions.explanation: More training data is generally the most effective remedy for overfitting because it provides more evidence of the true underlying pattern and makes it harder for the model to memorize noise. The other options (removing regularization, training longer, increasing complexity) would all make overfitting worse.
